data.speaker: polly
data.text: SQUAWK! Manya, you look so EXCITED. That's because the village is EXCITING! We must use the right Adjective suffixes to express feelings and causes!

rules.title: FEELINGS vs. CAUSES: The ING/ED Rule
rules.formula: The feeling uses -ED | The cause uses -ING
rules.explainA: Use **-ed** (past participle) to describe how a person (or duck, cat, etc.) feels, or their emotional state. *Example: We were bored.*
rules.explainB: Use **-ing** (present participle) to describe the person, thing, or situation that causes the feeling. *Example: The lesson was boring.*
rules.teacherNote: PLE TRAP: If the subject is a person, they are usually **-ed**. If the subject is an event, place, or thing, it is usually **-ing**.

data.text: I forgot my boots in the city! If I had remembered my boots, I would not have dirtied my feet. This is the **Conditional Type 3**, the rule of **Regret**!

rules.title: THE FORMULA OF PAST REGRET
rules.formula: If + Subject + HAD + V3 ... Subject + WOULD HAVE + V3
rules.explainA: The condition uses the **Past Perfect** tense (had + past participle) to state the impossible past action.
rules.explainB: The result uses **would have** + past participle to state the impossible consequence.
rules.teacherNote: PLE TRAP: This is used to talk about things that **DID NOT** happen in the past. You can also use **could have** or **might have** instead of **would have**.

data.speaker: kiki
data.text: Look at me! I am cooking the food. In the Passive Voice, we say: The food is being cooked by me! Always focus on the **object**!

data.topicTitle: Rule: Active vs. Passive Voice (Present Continuous)

rules.title: THE 'BEING' CONTINUOUS SHIFT
rules.formula: Active: S + is/are + V-ing + O  -> Passive: O + is/are + BEING + V3 + by S
rules.exampleA: The workers are building a new classroom.
rules.exampleB: A new classroom is being built by the workers.
rules.explainA: The focus is on the **Doer** (workers). The structure is simple continuous.
rules.explainB: The focus is on the **Object** (classroom). We insert **BEING** before the V3 (past participle).
rules.teacherNote: UNEB loves 'being' in the continuous passive voice! Always remember: **'being' is for continuous, 'been' is for perfect**.

The village market was a **bustling** and **exciting** place. Goods **were being sold** by many vendors. Polly was fascinated by the way the vendors spoke. Kiki, who was bored by the long **scrutiny** of the baskets, only wanted to buy some fish.

PASSAGE 3: A Lesson in Humility

Manya had scoffed at the idea of **chores**, thinking they were **exhausting** and beneath him. He was quickly **chastened** when he saw his grandmother, frail but determined, **washing** all the family clothes by hand. If he **had not seen** her working so hard, he **might have refused** to help. He felt a deep sense of humility and spent the rest of the day enthusiastically helping with the farming **routine**.

The **bash** was finally set up on the final evening. The **planning** had been extensive. The whole village was **invited**. Before leaving, Manya promised his grandparents that he would **revise** his entire syllabus before the new term **commenced**.
